issues.title: [Bug]: method parameter named 'self is accepted instead of "redeclared symbol"
issues.edge_case_reason: needs a quoted-identifier parameter named 'self in a method
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Clean-context spec review: 'self is the identifier self (quoted identifiers), and self is already bound in a method body (§6.8.1.2), so the parameter's scope overlaps and it must be a redeclaration error. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. Related but distinct: #1659 (self in parameter default), #1562 (self in field initializer).

issues.title: [Bug]: BIR pretty printer prints `unknown` for `===` and `!==`
issues.output: --dump-bir shows `%1 = unknown %3 %5;` and `%8 = unknown %10 %12;` for === and !==
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: bir/pretty_print.go falls back to "unknown" (line 615) for exact equality. Dumped BIR misrepresents the source -> frontend (BIR tooling). Issue reproducer is the corpus program subset1/01-misc/equal-v (a statement quoted in the issue); I wrote a full program. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: isolated class doesn't check non-private fields brought in by object-type inclusion
issues.edge_case_reason: isolated class combined with object-type inclusion of a mutable field
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec review: an isolated class's non-isolated fields must be private (§8.6/§6.8.1.1); included field xs is public, non-final, int[] -> must be rejected. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. No duplicate (nearest #1711, #1503).

issues.title: [Bug]: toString of a deeply nested value aborts the process with a Go stack overflow
issues.output:
built
runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit
fatal error: stack overflow (exit 2)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Concerns lang.value toString (values.String/toStringNested recursion) -> langlib. Spec review: the spec defines the result (prints built then 4000002) and is silent on resource limits, but an untrappable process abort fits no part of the spec's error model; treat as a robustness bug (normal result preferred, trappable panic acceptable). Related: #1703, #1697 (other stack overflows), not duplicates.

issues.title: [Bug]: computed mapping key of type string:Char gives value expected type never
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected never, got 1 --> 1719.bal:4:24
issues.edge_case_reason: computed mapping key whose static type is string:Char
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec review: for map<int> the inherent type gives int as the expected type for every field value (§6.7.2 mapping constructor), so the program is valid and should print {"a":1}. Valid program rejected -> frontend. No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: non-readonly class or object type can include a readonly class
issues.edge_case_reason: object-type inclusion of a readonly class into a non-readonly class/object type
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec review: §5.6.3.8 allows inclusion only of a class with no readonly qualifier, with the §8.6 exception only for readonly classes; both *Point lines must be errors. Missing diagnostic -> frontend. Related (opposite direction) #1287; not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: init method declaration rules not enforced (private init, return type without nil accepted)
issues.output: first program prints 1, second prints true; both exit 0 with no diagnostic
issues.edge_case_reason: plain class init declarations (private init / returns error)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. Spec review: §6.8.1.5 says init visibility cannot be private and its return type must contain nil; both programs must be rejected. Missing diagnostics -> frontend. Related #1297 (calling non-public initializers), not a duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: compiler crash (nil CompilerContext in xmlParser) on an XML template attribute without a quoted value
issues.output:
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV] context.(*CompilerContext).addDiagnostic(0x0,...) context/context.go:268 <- parser.(*xmlParser).parseXMLCharacterSet xml_parser.go:448
issues.edge_case_reason: malformed XML template with an unquoted interpolated attribute value
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: parser panics (nil CompilerContext) while trying to report an internal error. Spec review: §6.6.2 / XML AttValue must be quoted, so it should be a syntax error, never a crash. Front-end Go panic -> frontend + frontend-crash. No duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: compiler crash (nil pointer in semtypes.newFieldPairs) when an included method is overridden with a return type of the class itself
issues.output:
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV] semtypes.newFieldPairs field_pair.go:165 <- intersectMapping mapping_ops.go:141 <- mappingFormulaIsEmpty
issues.edge_case_reason: common pattern: class including an object type (e.g. object:Iterable) whose iterator() returns self
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: front end panics during class type resolution. Spec review: override return type C is a subtype of object {} (§5.6.3.8), so it must compile and print true. frontend + frontend-crash. Possibly same root cause as #1204/#1295 (nil in mappingFormulaIsEmpty on recursive types), but different trigger; not marked duplicate.

issues.title: [Bug]: runtime crash (nil pointer dereference) after `trap checkpanic` inside a nested block
issues.output:
error("bad")
error: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
        at main(1707.bal:12)
issues.edge_case_reason: trap wrapping an inline checkpanic inside a nested block
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main. The dumped BIR is wrong: the checkpanic lowering emits `PopScopeFrame` before `panic %7` (bb4) inside the trap's error-table range [bb2,bb6]->bb7, so after the trap the block's scope frame is gone and `(1, i)` dereferences nil. `trap (10 / z)` in the same position emits no PopScopeFrame and works. BIR incorrect -> frontend. Spec review: trap turns the checkpanic panic into the value, then execution continues (prints error("bad") then 1). Possibly related #1468 (trap around query, runtime label), not a duplicate.
